content:
julia.cs: Hey team — our app started getting a ton of 429s hitting the Dedicated pool this morning (~09:07 UTC). Example trace id: trace_0a9f3, customer tenant id: tenant-889. Errors look like rate limit exceeded. Latency also spiked to 3-5s for some requests. Can you help?
sarah.support: Sorry about that, julia. Can you share a short repro (curl) and whether you're on Dedicated Standard or Private? Also any recent config changes in the console? :eyes:
julia.cs: We're on Dedicated Standard in us-west. No changes from our side. Minimal repro: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"text-serve-1","input":"hi","max_tokens":10}' (we hit 429s after ~60 req/min)
mike.oncall: Jumping in — looking at infra metrics now. I see per-tenant throttles ramping up at 09:06 UTC matching julia's uuid. KV cache & GPU queue depth look fine. Autoscaler didn't spawn extra pods because pool was already at max_instances=4. But per-tenant rate limiter was rejecting: tenant-889 was at 120 RPM cap.
sarah.support: 120 RPM seems low if the customer bursts. Is that a tenant-level default?
alex.eng: That 120 RPM came from a quota record created via the admin UI last year. UI stored it as "120" but the backend expects RPS. We have a units mismatch bug: values entered as "per-minute" were interpreted as "per-second" in the rate-limit service. So 120 was applied as 120 RPS (=7200 RPM) or vice versa? I need to confirm: looking at audit logs now.
mike.oncall: Confirmed: rate-limiter config shows unit=second and value=2 for tenant-889 (interpreted from UI value 120 per-minute parsed incorrectly into 2 RPS). So customer effectively got a 2 RPS cap. That explains 429s and why autoscaler didn't help — throttling happens before queuing to the pool.
sarah.support: Ok that matches symptoms. Immediate question: can we bump the tenant cap temporarily so julia's traffic recovers while we fix the UI bug?
kevin-account: I'll notify the customer that we're escalating and will apply a temporary increase; want to avoid surprises.
alex.eng: We can patch via admin API. Hitting admin endpoint now:```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/tenant-889/quota" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"rate_limit_value":60,"rate_limit_unit":"minute"}'
```This should set 60 RPM. I'll apply and monitor.
deploy-bot: Patch request queued: PATCH-4387 (admin-quota-override) — scheduled immediate.
mike.oncall: Applied override at 09:22 UTC, admin returns 200. Monitoring now.
julia.cs: Seeing success immediately — 429s dropped to ~0 after 09:23 UTC, latency stabilized. Thanks.
sarah.support: Phew. We'll keep the override for 2 hours and then lower if all good. Alex, what's the root cause + long-term fix?
alex.eng: Root cause: admin UI accepts rate values in "per-minute" but the quota parser expects units in seconds. Miscommunication in the DTO — no schema validation. Fix: update admin UI to include explicit unit dropdown, add server-side unit validation, and add a migration to re-interpret stored tenant quotas where unit was omitted. I opened PR #4621 with tests.
kevin-account: I'll follow up with the customer with a brief incident summary and the mitigation we applied.
mike.oncall: Filing post-incident ticket and adding alert on per-tenant effective RPS<5 for Dedicated pools.
sarah.support: Notes for handoff: temporary override still active, PR #4621 will be reviewed by eng today, and product will decide whether to backfill historical tenant configs. Julia, please ping if you see anything odd in the next hour. :thumbsup:
julia.cs: All good for now. Appreciate the quick response!
